references.text: The Jubilee year was to be proclaimed, and everyone was to return to their property. This verse introduces the Jubilee year as the context for verse 13.
If a man could not redeem his property, it was to remain with the buyer until the Jubilee year, when it was to return to the original owner.
In the Jubilee year, an Israelite slave and his children were to go free and return to their clan and to their ancestral property.
In the Jubilee year, land that had been sold was to return to the original owner who had inherited it.
The Jubilee year is mentioned in connection with inheritance rights and the requirement that property remain within the tribe.
Ezekiel refers to the Jubilee year as the time when a gift of land was to return to the prince.
The prophecy about proclaiming liberty and a year of favor from the Lord is connected to the Jubilee principles of liberation and restoration.
